newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-COTTBUS BEAT KARLSRUHE 3-0 IN GERMAN CUP SEMIFINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COTTBUS BEAT KARLSRUHE 3-0 IN GERMAN CUP SEMIFINAL.

text.p: Lowly Cottbus Energie became only the second regional league side ever to reach the German Cup final by beating first division Karlsruhe 3-0 on Tuesday night.
Second half goals from Willi Kronhardt, Detlef Irrgang and Toralf Konetzke ensured Cottbus join Hertha Berlin in the German record books.
Cottbus will hope to go one better than the amateur Berlin side did in 1993 when they lost 1-0 to Bayer Leverkusen.
The east German side now meet either VfB Stuttgart or SV Hamburg -- who clash on Wednesday -- in the final.
Karlsruhe were in trouble after just 33 minutes when they were reduced to 10 men after Eduard Geyer was sent off for a foul.
Karlsruhe could have gone ahead two minutes later but naturalised German Sean Dundee's attempt was saved by Cotbuss 'keeper Kay Wehner.
Kronhardt's strike in the 65th minute was followed just three minutes later by Irrgang's goal and Konetzke sealed the win eight minutes from time.
"Although we are in the third league and Karlsruhe were the favourites, we showed we can play a little football," Cottbus trainer Eduard Geyer said after the match.
